title: Dissertation
text:
Tobler’s first law of geography states, “everything is related to everything else, but near things are more related than distant things” (Tobler 1970). I extend this principle to the analysis of the brain. My research lies at the intersection of spatial statistics and network analysis, with a primary focus on brain connectivity.
With the bold assumption that spatial structure itself encodes information about data behavior within the space, I analyze network data by focusing on neighborhood dependencies. More specifically, I use a Markov random field approach to address Tobler’s principle on single-subject brain network data.
My work is divided into the following three main areas.













Network


CAR


spdep


spatialreg



Integration of brain functional and structural networks using a conditional autoregressive model.




















Network


CAR


drunksc



Exploration of the contribution of graph structure to functional data behavior.
